clue.text: The time is at hand if one has this

definitions.text: The time is at hand if one has this

parts.words: The time is at hand if one has this
parts.note: read literally: whoever wears this device carries the hour on the arm, so the time is always within reach, at hand

explanation.surface: A saying that the moment is near, offered to someone who owns a certain item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The time is at hand' sounds like a prophecy that the moment has come; read literally it means the hour is shown near your hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A timepiece strapped at the joint above the hand puts the hour literally close to the hand.

clue.text: Yank is famous designer of cathedral and church

parts.note: Sir Christopher Wren designed St Paul's Cathedral in London

explanation.surface: An American who is a celebrated architect of cathedrals and churches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like a noun for an American; it is the verb, a sharp pull.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrench is to pull or twist something suddenly and violently.

clue.text: One American vehicle brought in — traveller with wings coming off

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a car is a road vehicle
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A traveller arrives in an American car, with some winged figure dropping out of the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Icarus flew on wings of feather and wax, which melted when he flew too near the sun, so they came off.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth Icarus flew on wax wings that melted near the sun and fell away, sending him into the sea.

clue.text: Flat not solid-looking as seen in scale model?

definitions.text: Flat not solid-looking as seen in scale model?

parts.words: Flat not solid-looking as seen in scale model?
parts.note: a drawing having only length and breadth, lacking depth, looks flat rather than solid, unlike a built miniature

explanation.surface: A flat that looks flimsy in the architect's model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment shown in an architect's model; it is the adjective meaning lacking depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something having only length and breadth, with no depth, appears flat and unsolid.

clue.text: A king, diminished man in a republic

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
gent is the shortened form of gentleman, a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A monarch reduced to an ordinary man living in a republic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diminished man' is GENT, gentleman cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a South American country governed as a republic.

clue.text: Impede crowd beginning to dash about wildly

indicators.note: beginning means just the first letter of crowd is taken

parts.note: ramp is an old verb meaning to rage or rush about violently, as in rampage

explanation.surface: Holding back a crowd as it starts to charge about in disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: RAMP in the sense of rampage, rushing about wildly, is an old word; C is the first letter of 'crowd'. 'crowd' wants to be CRAM; that leaves only P.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to restrict or hinder, as in cramping someone's style.

clue.text: A low type of singer

definitions.meaning: deep in pitch, as a sound at the bottom of the range
the male voice that sings the lowest part in a choir

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for deep sound and the name of the deepest male singing voice.

clue.text: A substance athlete mustn't take for a heavenly body

parts.note: anabolic steroids are banned performance-enhancing drugs in sport

explanation.surface: A banned drug an athlete must avoid, in exchange for a celestial object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky object orbiting the sun, a celestial body.

clue.text: Forwarded American coin in deposit

indicators.note: in places the coin within the word for forwarded

parts.note: forwarded mail has been sent on
a dime is the US ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: An American coin sent on and paid into an account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposit' looks like money paid into a bank; it is matter settling at the bottom of a liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sediment is the matter that settles out at the bottom of a liquid, a deposit.

clue.text: Possible power source met with reluctance — roar violently

indicators.note: violently suggests the letters of reluctance and roar are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A proposed power plant is greeted with reluctance and a furious outcry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violently' rearranges RELUCTANCE plus ROAR; 'met with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor generates heat for electricity, one possible source of power.

clue.text: Muse in wonder at opera

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words wonder at opera

explanation.surface: A muse marvelling at what she sees on the operatic stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points inside 'wonder at opera', where the letters ERATO run across the word breaks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she is one of the nine Muses, the one presiding over love poetry.

clue.text: Collected university certificate with marks at the side?

definitions.meaning: picked up one's degree, completing a course at university
describing a measuring vessel or ruler marked off in steps along its edge

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense: a measuring jug or scale is marked in regular steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means received a degree; the adjective describes a scale divided into measured intervals.

clue.text: Warning from one of the teaching unions I found in study

indicators.note: found in says the union and the letter I are placed inside the word for study

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn
AUT was the Association of University Teachers, a former British lecturers' union

explanation.surface: A warning issued by a teachers' union after a review.
explanation.walkthrough: The Association of University Teachers was a British lecturers' union, since merged; 'study' as a verb is the old word con.
explanation.definitionFit: A caution is a word of warning, an admonition to be careful.

clue.text: Rudeness about stern believer on journey

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for rudeness is read backwards

parts.note: lip is slang for cheeky backchat or impertinence
grim means stern, forbidding

explanation.surface: Someone's insolence prompts a severe reaction from a travelling worshipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the reversal signal, turning the cheeky backchat round before the word for stern follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrim is a person of faith who travels to a holy place.

clue.text: Thought it just might mean being deprived of freedom!

definitions.meaning: careful consideration, a weighing up of a matter

definitions.text: it just might mean being deprived of freedom!
definitions.meaning: split as ..., the prefix de- undoing liberation, i.e. losing one's freedom

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation flags a whimsical second reading: de- reverses a word, so removing liberation suggests being deprived of freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberation is long careful consideration; jokingly split, de-liberation suggests the opposite of being set free.

clue.text: Knight cantered excitedly around in raptures

indicators.note: around says the shuffled word goes round the knight's letter, enclosing it
excitedly means the letters of cantered are jumbled

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight gallops about in high excitement, delighted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' turns CANTERED into ENTRACED, and 'around' wraps it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Entranced means spellbound, filled with delight, as someone in raptures is.

clue.text: Exceptional English constable brought in as reinforcement

parts.note: a special constable is a volunteer part-time police officer in Britain, called on to support regular police

explanation.surface: An unusual English policeman drafted in to bolster the force.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a special, short for special constable, is a volunteer police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is a formal word for exceptional, out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Bungs something really excellent into ship

indicators.note: into says the excellent thing is placed inside the ship abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a topper is informal for something or someone outstanding

explanation.surface: Putting something first-rate aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bungs' looks like a verb, throws; it is the noun, plugs for holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bung is a plug for sealing a hole or bottle, as stoppers do.

clue.text: After short day at end of week is workplace OK?

parts.words: short day at end of week
parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday, a day at the end of the week
a factory is a place where people work

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether their workplace is acceptable after a shortened Saturday shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' only confirms the clue's order; 'OK?' is the definition, the question mark keeping the surface a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfactory means acceptable, good enough, all right.

clue.text: European refinement

definitions.meaning: from Poland, a central European country
elegance and finish in manners or style

explanation.definitionFit: The word names someone or something from Poland and also means elegant finish or sophistication.

clue.text: Make fun of death when immersed in drink

indicators.note: immersed in says the word for death goes inside the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in sips
end means death, as in meeting one's end

explanation.surface: Joking about mortality while drowning one's sorrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word; 'immersed in' is the container signal, sinking death inside a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is to parody or satirise, mocking someone by imitation.

clue.text: Former pilot bungled stunt maybe

parts.note: ex- means former, as in an ex-husband

indicators.note: bungled means messed up, so the letters of pilot are muddled

explanation.surface: A retired airman makes a mess of an aerobatic manoeuvre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungled' is the anagram signal for the letters of pilot, which follow the prefix for former.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a daring deed, of which a stunt is one kind; 'maybe' marks the example.

clue.text: Doctor, for instance, showing basis of legal claim

definitions.meaning: Dr is one example of an honorific placed before a name
the right to own property, as in holding the deeds to land

explanation.definitionFit: Doctor is an honorific placed before a name, and in law the word means the right of ownership.

clue.text: A hit with lyric in up-to-date style

parts.note: to lam is to strike or thrash
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A hit song with modern words, done in the latest fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is French, 'in the fashion', used in English for anything fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means in the current fashion, stylish and modern.

clue.text: A client is difficult and not flexible

indicators.note: difficult hints the letters are awkwardly arranged and must be sorted out

explanation.surface: A demanding customer who refuses to bend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges the letters of A CLIENT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inelastic does not stretch or give, so it is rigid and unbending.

clue.text: Attempted to get moored having crossed over river

indicators.note: having crossed says the word for moored straddles the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a boat that is moored is tied up
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A boat is tied up after making its way across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having crossed' puts R inside TIED; 'over' and 'to get' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tried means made an effort, had a go.

clue.text: Bank record

definitions.meaning: to bank is to tilt or lean over, as an aircraft or ship does
a written record set down item by item, such as a register

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a ship's lean to one side, like a plane banking, and also an itemised written roll.

clue.text: Newspaper article's trendy — it should offer authority

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's editorial article, plus the possessive S
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: An editorial on what is fashionable claims to speak with authority.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a leader is a newspaper's editorial.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadership is the power to direct others, the command that comes with being in charge.
